artifact: tools/roster.py — matches(), and the mutation pins on it in tools/tests/test_roster.py
finding: Two mutants of the predicate survive the whole suite and are left unpinned: normalising then .strip() on both sides, and normalising then .lower(). Each is behaviour-changing - an entry differing from its cell only in leading or trailing whitespace, or only in the case of one description word, fires under the shipped predicate and is forgiven under the mutant. Pinning every relaxation of a predicate nobody has proposed was judged unbounded work against a failure mode with no route into the tree, since the entry is generated from the cell and neither whitespace nor case drifts on its own.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- the decision-entry guards
finding: No check couples the [corrected] marker to its Erratum block. The lawfulness half is unreachable by any guard -- whether cited evidence truly falsifies a sentence is judgment -- and that half is not what this records; the marker-block biconditional is mechanical and uncovered. artifact: skills/adversarial-review/SKILL.md:41 -- the load-bearing-claim standard, as applied to universals

artifact: tools/lint.py -- the repository-wide walks: _iter_files, _python_files, and _prose_files

The remedy is determined -- one shared walk, or git ls-files -co --exclude-standard, which returns tracked plus untracked-not-ignored in a single call and removes the check-ignore round trip too -- but the walk was measured at 4ms of a 0.88s run, so the cost case for acting is absent and the duplication is the whole of the harm. artifact: tools/roster.py -- frontmatter()'s paragraph on the interior line endings it copies
finding: The sentence 'the committed bytes are the same wherever the generator last ran' is stated without the bound in_step states two functions down: git's text=auto refuses to normalise a file holding a lone carriage return, so a cell carrying one inside its frontmatter propagates it into the entry verbatim. Probed: such a cell and its entry both commit as i/-text. The only remedy adds a clause to the paragraph an experience session established, from real use, is the one a cold consumer reads and is turned by -- the consumer arrived with the wrong thesis and that paragraph corrected it -- and the bound is already stated in full, in the function whose job it is. Weight against a reader nobody has observed failing.
promotion: a session reuses frontmatter() outside the roster generator, or a report that a reader acted wrongly on the unqualified sentence, or the bound stops being stated on in_step.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- the message class for findings about the lint itself, being check-raised and check_emitted_ascii's unparseable-file branch
finding: check-raised states the situation and names no next step, so a session holding a red on the flow's mandated pre-commit gate is not told whether to file, re-run, or proceed. The claim that it is the only such message in the file was disproved: emitted-ascii's unparseable branch does the same, and is the same kind of message -- a report that the lint could not do its job rather than a report about the tree -- so check-raised follows a house pattern rather than breaking one. The remedy adds prose to a message an experience session established is untested by use, and if bought it covers both messages or neither.
promotion: a session reports being unable to act on a check-raised or unparseable-file finding, or a third message of this class is written, or either message is observed in use.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- check_committed_carriage_return's binary test
finding: The check skips binary content on a NUL in the first 8000 bytes, matched to git's own detection window so the two cannot disagree inside it. A binary whose first NUL falls past 8000 still classifies as i/-text, still has its bytes read, and still draws a finding whose remedy a reader cannot safely apply. The class is unclosable at this layer: git's own classification cannot separate such a file from a lone-carriage-return text file, which is the thing the check exists for. The remedy clause was softened to stop instructing a rewrite unconditionally; the misfire itself stands.
promotion: the first binary is tracked in this repository, or a finding is reported against a file whose text-ness the check cannot establish.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- _read_text's None, and what a check does with a file it cannot read
finding: _read_text returns None for 'binary, deliberately out of scope' and for 'could not be read' alike, so a caller cannot tell them apart and the mandated command can exit 0 over content it never examined -- the shape check_emitted_ascii's own message condemns. Distinguishing them changes a helper's contract with four consumers, which is a design call, and the docstring names two siblings (roster.is_generated, _git_ignored) that answer silently by design. The raising half was fixed; this is the silent half.
promotion: a third caller needs to tell the two apart, or a run is reported clean over content it could not read.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- check_stdio_wired's finding message on the module-attribute call spelling
finding: A module that imports winio both ways -- `import winio` and a redundant `from winio import utf8_stdio` -- and calls winio.utf8_stdio() as the first statement of main() is reported as 'defines main() and does not call it first', because the check requires first.value.func be an ast.Name. The redundant from-import is what makes the message wrong rather than merely loose: with `import winio` alone the guard reports 'neither imports nor calls it first', since it scans only ast.ImportFrom. Probed on both spellings; the external reviewer caught this entry naming the second case's spelling against the first case's message. The call is first; the diagnosis names the wrong defect and the remedy prescribes what is already done. Message-only, but it is a code change and #252's affirmed boundary excluded changes to this guard. Bound: the misdiagnosis needs a redundant from-import present; the pure module-import spelling gets a loose message with a working remedy.
promotion: a session follows the misdiagnosis and edits ordering that is already correct, or the guard is opened for another reason.

artifact: skills/substrate/references/text-mode.md -- rule 2's 'two properties'
finding: lib/winio.py sets three: encoding, newline suppression, and errors='replace', the last because a guard that dies encoding its own failure message converts a legible failure into a traceback. A reader discharging exactly the two the rule names gets rc=1, empty stdout and UnicodeEncodeError on a surrogate filename byte -- the failure the same file describes two sections down -- reachable on Linux CI via surrogateescape. Originated by #252's defense and reproduced by its judge. Not fixed there because the remedy has two shapes, a third property in the headline or a bound in the helper-less branch, and picking trades against the rule's new strength of being exactly two.

artifact: skills/substrate/references/text-mode.md -- rule 2's 'a version-stamped path that stops resolving at the next release'
finding: A plugin cache does not promptly stop resolving. Measured on one machine: of the two plugins that have ever been updated, both retained the older version directory (tradecraft across 98 minutes, agent-orchestra across four days), and the day's in-use sweep removed neither; 0.37.0 still resolved six days and seventeen releases on. The two claims that decide the clause are sound though: the decisive reason is on the shipped surface one clause earlier as the within-reach test, and the plugin-installed seat of PR #252's second experience session read this clause, called the reasoning visibly true, and wrote both properties itself rather than reaching for a cache path. Not fixed because replacing it means asserting something true about cache eviction, which is a design call, and deleting it removes something a reader reported as useful.
promotion: a reader reaches for a cache path, or a change makes this clause load-bearing -- in particular removal or weakening of the within-reach test that currently carries the branch.

artifact: skills/substrate/references/text-mode.md -- rule 2's helper-less branch, folded with the 'two properties' entry above

PR #252's second experience session: the seat with the plugin on disk did not hit this because it could read winio.py, and the seat with prose alone confirmed the newline half by capturing bytes rather than by reading anything shipped. artifact: tools/check_version_bump.py -- the untracked-file enumeration on a tree without .gitignore
finding: The guard enumerates untracked files with git ls-files --others --exclude-standard, which honours .gitignore. The message is confident and specific and gives no hint the files are build artifacts, so the likely resolution is a version bump shipped for a repo-only change. No live instance here -- this repository tracks .gitignore and the guard reports one shipped file. Observed by an experience-session consumer against a tree whose isolation had dropped the file, which is how the class surfaced at all.

artifact: skills/adversarial-review/references/the-record.md -- the route from a closing session to the ranking the `value` key cites

artifact: skills/substrate/references/text-mode.md -- text mode when a stage measures rather than writes
finding: Three stages in one review each stated a wrong length for the very field under review, from one cause: `git show` piped through a text-mode decode under cp1252 inflates each em-dash by two characters. In PR #269's panel, `operational` and `cold-read` both reported the description as 499 -> 574 or 499 -> 572 against the guard's 497 -> 572, and the defense reproduced 499 -> 572 (+73) and was about to file it against the merge before catching itself; `cold-read` reconciled its own figure unprompted. The correct figure reproduces only under an explicit UTF-8 decode, and matches `check_cell_frontmatter`'s. The cell teaches this class for a script's output and its line endings; nothing routes a stage that is *measuring* a figure to it, so the standard to derive a correction from its source is satisfied while the source is read through a lossy copy.

artifact: tools/check_version_bump.py -- the tip bound when --base names a revision that is its own merge base
finding: Passing an explicit merge-base sha to --base makes tip == base, so the second bound is arithmetically vacuous and the run returns exit 0 on the #110 collision with no indication that only one bound was applied. --help promises the version must exceed both. The spelling is already in this repository's vocabulary: .github/workflows/ci.yml documents `--base $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)` for a sibling tool. Not fixed: the only remedy requires the guard to distinguish 'the base has not moved' from 'you named the merge base', which _resolve_base cannot currently express and which test_a_branch_level_with_its_base_is_unaffected asserts must print nothing.

artifact: .github/workflows/ci.yml -- the pull_request checkout the version guard runs against
finding: On a freshly-computed refs/pull/N/merge, merge-base(HEAD, origin/main) equals the base tip, so the second bound is arithmetically vacuous in CI and a #110 collision reds through the first bound only; the act-shaped message the change was built to deliver never reaches a CI log. Checking out github.event.pull_request.head.sha would restore it. Not fixed: PR #270's affirmed boundary names ci.yml as not touched, CI still reds so no unlawful change passes, and once the conditional unit clause landed the message CI prints is honest. A stale merge ref, which is the shape #119 recorded as 'CI passed', does exercise the second bound.
promotion: a session diagnosing a version collision from a CI log and being sent the wrong way by it, or an owner asking why CI's diagnosis differs from the local one.

artifact: tools/check_version_bump.py -- the base version read when the base has no manifest at all

An adoption pull request of the shape the word describes -- the manifest alongside the skills being adopted -- still returns exit 2 from the base version read, whose trailer names an act ('repair the manifest it could not read') that cannot be performed, because the branch's manifest is fine. artifact: tools/check_version_bump.py -- the no-bump FAIL's prescribed target on a stale remote-tracking base
finding: The only message that prescribes a version number derived from the base ref's tip carries no freshness disclosure, structurally, in both polarities of the fetch state -- so on a clone one fetch behind it names 'past <stale version>' with nothing saying the number came from a possibly stale read. Bounded: acting on it reaches the PASS, which does disclose, so the cost is one guard cycle rather than a shipped collision. Not fixed: the remedy is a clause appended to the tail of the guard's most-printed FAIL, and an experience-session consumer's echo of that same message stopped three sentences in, before the remedy -- the words would land in the region measured as unread, on the sentence a sustained high was simultaneously making actionable.
promotion: a session acting on the stale-derived target and reaching a shipped collision rather than one wasted cycle, or evidence that the PASS's freshness clause is itself not reaching readers.

artifact: tools/check_version_bump.py -- _manifest_at's ref-side read and _git's lossy decode
finding: The ref side of _manifest_at reads the manifest blob through _git, which decodes with errors='replace', while the working-tree side diagnoses a non-UTF-8 manifest explicitly. So a base manifest that is not UTF-8 is answered from substituted characters rather than reported, and a branch that re-encodes the same copy as UTF-8 and changes nothing else is told a carried field changed. Bounded: a false PASS is unreachable, because the strict current-side read fires exit 2 first. Not fixed: _git's lossy decode exists so a non-UTF-8 path cannot kill the guard and is shared by five callers, so the remedy must add a second strict read path and a rule about which read to use -- a standing obligation on later sessions out of proportion to a false FAIL on a re-encode.
promotion: a manifest that is actually non-UTF-8 at a base ref, or a second site where _git's lossy decode changes an answer rather than a message.

artifact: tools/check_version_bump.py -- the guard when a version decrement lands on the base ref
finding: Two coupled defects, one reachable only through the other. (a) A manifest edit touching only `version` yields an empty touched set and returns PASS 'no shipped-zone change to version' -- including when the version went DOWN, so a decrement landing alone on the base ref is passed rather than refused. (b) That is the precursor for the moved-base arm, which is entered whenever tip != base and new <= old and says nothing about top: when top < new <= old its clause ('carrying X, which this branch has not risen above') is false and its target ('past X') is below the bound the guard actually applies, which is the merge-base version. Verified by fixture: raising to 0.5.1 and then 0.6.0 as the message instructs both re-enter the same arm with the same target -- the named act does not terminate, which is the class PR #270's first post-fix cycle graded high, surviving in the arm that cycle's remedy did not reach. Not fixed: the moved-arm remedy is five lines with measured zero regression surface but is unpinned, so it owes a fixture built on a state with zero instances in 58 manifest-touching commits; and the decrement limb's remedy decides whether the guard polices version monotonicity independent of any shipped-zone change, a semantic call outside that change's affirmed boundary.
promotion: a version decrement actually landing on the base ref of any repository running this guard, or any run reaching the moved arm with the base tip carrying a version below the merge base.

artifact: skills/adversarial-review/references/roster.md -- the standing instruction that every seat rules on carried recorded findings
finding: The instruction is discharged by every seat against every carried entry, matched to the artifact rather than to a seat's lens, so a four-seat round carrying two entries produces eight rulings of two questions. PR #270's round one produced seven `untouched` rulings across three seats and the judge, on two entries, with no divergence and one live reproduction that still did not promote; its post-fix cycles produced none at all, the post-fix look not being a seat. Not fixed, and NOT a case for retiring the instruction -- repeated `untouched` is the record instrument working, and retiring the standing read would leave entries written by closing stages and read by nobody, which is the failure the fetch-at-assignment rule exists to prevent. What is unestablished is the width: whether the entries are better ruled once per round by the stage best placed than once per seat. The remedy edits a shipped cell and decides which stage rules, so it is neither determined nor inside any change's boundary here, and one review is one occasion.
promotion: a second panel review producing a round of identical `untouched` rulings across every seat on the same carried entries, or an entry promoted by a seat that no other stage of that review would have reached.
